title: Cold calling 3hrs, non stop

segments.summary: Student Seamster's followup call to Rosalind (Hazel Park MI agent) — $70K offer on $90K Chrysler Drive flip. Demonstrates section-8 deal analyzer math, why $70K vs $90K with $1434 rent. Soft sell + 'should have asked for her other listings.'

Wholesale negotiation w/ Turner St Detroit agent. Richard tries to flip-buy, agent says 70K bottom. Pivots brilliantly: 'let me wholesale it for 7 days, you keep listing live, cancel if you get better offer.' Agent agrees. Then cross-pitches Clover Lawn nearby. KEY MOVE: turning a 'no' into a free wholesale arrangement.

Yousef's San Antonio Vargas St deal — seller owes $174K @ 1025/mo, rent $2400. Richard math-checks live, decides $30K to take over debt (no monthly payments — no room). Reaches voicemail. Pivots strategy from hybrid to high-DP mortgage takeover.

Kai's TN triplex (Highland Ave) — seller Michael's counter: $315K, $25K down, takeover $238K, $52K seller financed @ 6%, 5yr balloon. On live with seller, then seller asks if recorded → asks to take call offline. Rare moment of friction with sellers + privacy.

Jordan in chat challenges Garn-St-Germain do-on-sale clause. Richard defends 'add-to-trust' model — owner-leases-portion to investor for compliance. Tries to summon attorney Jeff Hatcher live. Best deep legal explanation of why his trust structure works.

Live underwrites why Kai's Highland Ave triplex doesn't work — 2800 rent vs ~2400 payment after T&I, no room for SF payments. Coaches the 'I'd have to hold you at gunpoint' framework for showing sellers their deal is dead.

Lamel: 'hidden duplex' advertised as single-family. Richard live-comps via PropStream/Zillow, identifies it as risky flip (4000sqft = too much surface for things to go wrong). Recommends $40K offer. Then shows what GOOD flip candidates look like — windows new = green light. Best flipper-evaluation tutorial in the video.

Angel's Florida deal — no rentals in area + no recent investor sales. Richard demonstrates 'first-flip-in-area = no buyer.' Teaches how to tell investor flip from family sale (LVP floors, gray paint, blue doors, professional photos).
Quick call to Oregon mobile home park buyer — $2M Coos Bay park asking 30% down SF. Buyer max is 10%. Sets up Richard's lowball strategy.
Crexi mobile-home-park hunt + voicemails to Dimmitri/Jennifer. 'I do 3-5 deals/month, 20-25 in closing right now.' Shows the live process of cold-texting park owners with starting offer figures.

Inbound submission: Cleveland OH turnkey, $100K mortgage @ 3% on $215K property. Richard live-pitches: $20K down, $215K above-market, 7yr term, $300/mo to seller. Seller counters $30K down; Richard counter-counters $25K + closing costs (32K effective). Negotiated 'real-money on table' framing — honest about realtor vs creative. Masterful MT pitch from a real inbound.

Live Lightning Leads hunt across Aurora CO, Denver, Dallas, San Antonio, Tyler TX. Discusses why ultra-low-equity 2% rate properties no longer exist post-2024. Filters live for sweet-spot equity (~25-35% gap) and rent-to-PITI ratios. Practical lead-source tutorial.

Three live cold-call attempts on TX multifamilies. Dallas quadplex (taxes alone $1200/mo = killed), Tyler TX duplex (rent-to-PITI too tight), San Antonio Shali Ave (auto-attendant brokerage gauntlet). Demonstrates qualifying-out via math in real time. Textbook 'most calls die, keep going.'

Live comp/ARV exercise on $67K Detroit flip candidate. Step-by-step: find renovated comps in same square-footage band, calc price-per-sqft, exclude outliers, multiply against subject. Lands at $165K ARV, $40K rehab, $75K offer. Emails dual cash/SF offer template — best 'how to build an offer' moment.

Harry Gold (buyer) callback: shares Richard's pipeline ('2 triplexes, duplex, quadplex under contract, 2 duplexes more'). Harry passes on a particular single-family — no electric meter = guaranteed rewire.

Anti-hater proof flex: walks through every fix-flip + wholesale deal in pipeline, leaks agent phone numbers for verification ($220K next month). Shows driver's license matching LLC ownership on public record. Drops $2.558M trailing 12-mo revenue figure. Long but valuable proof-of-business segment.
Harry's quick feedback on Saed's single-family flip: 'lower risk but not enough meat — $20-30K profit ceiling, need $30K min.' Sets the flipper's profit-floor rule.
Closing rant: fix-flip checks $66K + $44K week apart. Why even ONE flip/year replaces W2 income. 'Time > money.' Worth a listen — pure motivation.

summary: Less dense than video 1 — only 1 real deal locked (Turner St wholesale arrangement at start). Mostly underwriting/coaching + cold-call voicemails. Best moments: Turner-St wholesale jiu-jitsu (0:11-0:18), Cleveland MT inbound (1:31-1:43), live ARV comp exercise (2:08-2:23). Skip 1:45-2:08 (lead-list filtering only — dry).
